newsitem.title: USA: Coke Enterprises buys two bottlers for $1.66 billion.
newsitem.headline: Coke Enterprises buys two bottlers for $1.66 billion.

text.p: Coca-Cola Enterprises, the giant Coke bottler, said Tuesday it agreed to pay about $1.66 billion to Coca-Cola Co. for its stakes in Coke bottlers in Canada and New York.
Coca-Cola Enterprises said it would acquire Coca-Cola Co.'s 48 percent stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Ltd of Canada and its 49 percent interest in Coca-Cola Bottling Co. of New York Inc.

Henry Schimberg, president and chief operating officer of Coca-Cola Enterprises, said his company pursued the acquisitions because of "significant volume growth and margin improvement opportunities" in the Canadian and New York markets.
The Atlanta-based bottler said it agreed to pay C$17, or about $12.25, for each of the 19.6 million shares of the Canadian Coke bottler held by Coca-Cola Co.

Coca-Cola Enterprises said it also plans to make an offer for approximately 52 percent of Coke Canada held by the public at C$19.50, or $14, a share in cash. This represents a premium of about 20 percent over the average closing price of Coke Canada's shares for the last four weeks, it said.

In January 1994 Coca-Cola Enterprises bought 4 percent of Coke New York from The Coca-Cola Co., along with a five-year right of first refusal on Coke's remaining 49 percent investment in Coke New York and an option to negotiate for this ownership interest after two years.
It said it intends to acquire the remaining 47 percent of Coke New York currently held by private investors.
Coca-Cola Enterprises said it expects to complete the deals by the end of September.
Coca-Cola Beverages Ltd. operates in all 10 Canadian provinces, reaching a population of 27 million people, and represents 95 percent of The Coca-Cola Co.'s unit case volume in Canada.
Based on current currency exchange rates, Coke Canada generated 1996 net operating revenues of approximately $690 million on 259 million unit cases.

The Coca-Cola Bottling Co. of New York Inc. operates in the New York metropolitan area, certain other areas in the state of New York, and in parts of Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, and Vermont, serving a population of 24 million.
Coke New York sold 214 million unit cases in 1996, producing net operating revenues of about $744 million.
Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc. is the world's largest bottler of non-alcoholic beverages, distributing more than 58 percent of Coca-Cola Co.'s U.S. bottle and can volume.
It is also the sole licensed bottler for Coke products in Belgium, Britain, the Netherlands and most of France.
